source_summary.author_line: By William Saville, also known as The Transgender T-Rex #TheTransgenderTRex
source_summary.revision_note: Expanded the original v1 shell into a generator-ready alignment model using the attached full guide.

core_philosophy.summary: Belavadös treats alignment as a living moral profile rather than a fixed label.
core_philosophy.design_goal: Track selfishness, lawfulness, cooperation, and honor as independent axes so characters can grow, fail, recover, and surprise the table.
core_philosophy.dm_rule: Use alignment as a living reputation system, not a punishment system. Award points only when actions meaningfully affect story, relationships, faction standing, moral consequences, or character identity.
core_philosophy.fairness_rule: If the table can explain the award in one sentence, the award is probably clear enough. If it takes five sentences, log the moment and settle it later.

phases.name: Extreme negative
phases.meaning: Strongly skewed to the negative end. Often feared, avoided, distrusted, or opposed

phases.name: Skewed negative
phases.meaning: Leaning negative but still flexible. NPC reactions are mixed

phases.name: Neutral or balanced
phases.meaning: The true center. Stable, adaptable, and open to many paths

phases.name: Skewed positive
phases.meaning: Leaning positive. Trusted by like-minded NPCs and seen as dependable

phases.name: Extreme positive
phases.meaning: Fully committed to the positive end. Revered or hated for strong conviction

axes.name: Altruism
axes.core_question: Does the character give or take?
axes.measures: Willingness to prioritize others vs self-interest

scale.description: Selflessness, compassion, and sacrifice versus selfish ambition and exploitation

axes.name: Lawfulness
axes.core_question: Does the character submit to structure or break away?
axes.measures: Relationship to rules, systems, and authority

scale.description: Obedience to structure, rules, and duty versus rebellion and personal freedom

axes.name: Cooperation
axes.core_question: Does the character build with others or work alone?

scale.description: Group harmony, loyalty, and teamwork versus independence and self-interest

axes.name: Honor
axes.core_question: Does the character keep an internal code when unobserved?
axes.measures: Personal integrity and consistency of values

scale.description: Integrity, truth, principles, and restraint versus deceit and ruthless pragmatism

profile_label_matrix.note: Profile labels are appendix labels. Axis prose still describes low Honor as dishonorable/ruthless, while profile names use Pragmatic for the low-honor slot.

trait_definitions.meaning: Usually means high Altruism and often high Honor

design_interpretation.explanation: Characters are not restricted to rigid alignment boxes
Lawful thief, rebellious saint, or selfish protector are all valid
Enables more honest and nuanced character descriptions
The setting recognizes and reacts to these mixed moral traits as normal combinations

threshold_translations.requirement: Low Altruism and usually low Honor
A cursed blade that once required evil alignment might instead require Altruism below 800 and Honor below 1000. A holy relic may require Altruism above 2200 and Honor above 2000.

old_alignment_conversion.new_question: Does the character respect rules and structure, or reject them?
old_alignment_conversion.watch_for: Look at promises, laws, hierarchy, rebellion, and consistency.

old_alignment_conversion.new_question: Does the character work with people or go their own way?
old_alignment_conversion.watch_for: Look at party loyalty, teamwork, solo action, and group reliability.

old_alignment_conversion.new_question: Does the character keep an internal code even when no one is watching?
old_alignment_conversion.watch_for: Look at honesty, vows, duels, trustworthiness, and shame.

logic.fit_award: Use when a choice is on-brand for the character's current profile.
logic.shift_award: Use when a choice genuinely changes the character's direction.
logic.same_scene_rule: A single scene can earn both only when both parts are true.

optional_rules.rule: Cap alignment rewards at one award per axis per scene unless the scene has clearly separated beats.
Give no award for choices made only to farm points.

optional_rules.rule: A simple session tracker makes the system easier to run. I write down the scene, the axis affected, why it mattered, and the fit and shift awards I plan to hand out.

entries.name: Lawful Renegade
entries.description: A rebel in legal robes. They bend laws to suit their gain while pretending to be team players - calculating, efficient, and just manipulative enough to get ahead.

entries.name: Lawful Drifter
entries.description: Follows the rules just enough to survive. Doesn't stick around long, but won't burn bridges either. A ghost with a code.

entries.name: Lawful Champion
entries.description: Seeks glory under the banner of law. Noble in words, loyal to allies - yet always with an eye on personal legacy.

entries.name: Lawful Strategist
entries.description: A master planner of the long game. Coldly loyal, ruthlessly efficient, and always thinking ten steps ahead.

entries.name: Lawful Knave
entries.description: Keeps just enough law to stay out of jail. A slippery operator who toes the line without any deeper loyalties.

entries.name: Lawful Avenger
entries.description: Enforces personal justice like a holy wrathblade. Rules are tools, not ideals - they punish to feed their pride.

entries.name: Lawful Mercenary
entries.description: A sword for hire with contracts tattooed on their soul. Lawful only when paid, but never sloppy.

entries.name: Lawful Marauder
entries.description: Wears structure like armor while carving a bloody path. Not cruel - just committed to their own violent climb.

entries.name: Lawful Gladiator
entries.description: Upholds combat as ceremony. Respects tradition and fair fights - but glory and personal honor always come first.

entries.name: Neutral Renegade
entries.description: Works with others only when needed. Often a necessary evil in group efforts - smart, ruthless, and tolerated.

entries.name: Neutral Drifter
entries.description: A wanderer with just enough charm to stay welcome. Avoids attachment but doesn't actively sabotage it.

entries.name: Neutral Champion
entries.description: Fights for group causes - until the applause fades. Their heroism is real... but so is their thirst for praise.

entries.name: Neutral Strategist
entries.description: Thinks only in outcomes, not morals. Moves quietly, makes power plays, and always walks away with more.

entries.name: Neutral Knave
entries.description: A wildcard with no compass. Acts on impulse or opportunity - sometimes helpful, often a headache.

entries.name: Neutral Avenger
entries.description: Revenge is their religion. Morality isn’t the goal - just evening the score, no matter who gets in the way.

entries.name: Neutral Mercenary
entries.description: No gods. No masters. Just coin and contract. Brutal, blunt, and fiercely independent in battle.

entries.name: Neutral Marauder
entries.description: Fights not for principle, but power. They don’t pick sides - only targets.

entries.name: Neutral Gladiator
entries.description: Honors the duel, not the war. Cares deeply about reputation and performance, not cause or creed.

entries.name: Chaotic Renegade
entries.description: A team-friendly anarchist with their own goals. Helps the group... until they don’t.

entries.name: Chaotic Drifter
entries.description: A storm with a smile. Allies when it’s fun, disappears when it’s not. Hard to hate - but harder to trust.

entries.name: Chaotic Champion
entries.description: A rebel hero - dramatic, bold, magnetic. Loyal in the moment, but always the star of their own tale.

entries.name: Chaotic Strategist
entries.description: Unpredictable mastermind. Seeks chaos only they understand, playing both sides to win.

entries.name: Chaotic Knave
entries.description: Pure mischief incarnate. Chaos is its own reward - no loyalty, no plan, just vibes.

entries.name: Chaotic Avenger
entries.description: Burns worlds to avenge one wound. Justice isn’t blind - it’s furious.

entries.name: Chaotic Mercenary
entries.description: A volatile warrior for hire. May switch sides mid-fight if the pay’s better or the thrill is stronger.

entries.name: Chaotic Marauder
entries.description: Wrecks, raids, and rages with zero remorse. No ideology - just destruction.

entries.name: Chaotic Gladiator
entries.description: Fights like it’s performance art. Theatrics, blood, and brutal showdowns define them.

entries.name: Neutral Operator
entries.description: A practical team player. Gets things done with minimal drama and maximum efficiency. Doesn’t care about glory - just results.

entries.name: Neutral Collaborator
entries.description: Goes with the flow. A team member who supports without leading or resisting - blends in, stabilizes chaos.

entries.name: Neutral Harmonizer
entries.description: Balances relationships with grace. A quiet peacemaker, not for recognition, but because harmony matters.

entries.name: Neutral Adapter
entries.description: A true survivalist. Adjusts to any situation without strong ties or ideals. The embodiment of flexible neutrality.

entries.name: Neutral Ethicist
entries.description: A quiet moral compass. Doesn’t preach, but always chooses the path that harms the fewest - even in stillness.

entries.name: Neutral Ravager
entries.description: Battles only when needed. Efficient, deadly, and never dramatic. Violence is just another tool.

entries.name: Neutral Scoundrel
entries.description: A fighter without a cause. May brawl for coin, pride, or boredom - but rarely cares who wins the war.

entries.name: Neutral Warrior
entries.description: Wields strength as its own code. Neutral in belief, yet bound by a personal oath of fair combat and protection.

entries.name: Lawful Coordinator
entries.description: A mission-first peacemaker. Brings order and aid to the many, solving problems with a balanced, sensible hand.

entries.name: Lawful Mediator
entries.description: A fair voice in the storm. Listens before acting, judges without ego, and restores peace without personal gain.

entries.name: Lawful Guardian
entries.description: The steadfast protector of the realm. Uplifts the weak, obeys the law, and inspires trust with every step.

entries.name: Lawful Defender
entries.description: A shield with purpose. Puts others first, but doesn’t waste time with idealism. Efficiently defends what matters.

entries.name: Lawful Arbiter
entries.description: Seeks justice without bias. Mediates with detachment, but never loses sight of the greater good.

entries.name: Lawful Sentinel
entries.description: The silent watcher. Their loyalty is unwavering, their purpose pure - they serve to protect, not to be seen.

entries.name: Lawful Enforcer
entries.description: Justice with an edge. Enforces order for the benefit of all - even if it means breaking bones to preserve peace.

entries.name: Lawful Vigilante
entries.description: Operates in shadows for the light. Defends the helpless but trusts fists over courts. A silent justice.

entries.name: Lawful Crusader
entries.description: A warrior of divine duty. Law and mercy guide their blade. Fights not for conquest - but for righteousness.

entries.name: Neutral Coordinator
entries.description: Helps where help is needed. Doesn’t seek control, just solutions. A reliable team lead who lifts others quietly.

entries.name: Neutral Mediator
entries.description: A calming presence. Bridges gaps between factions, friends, and foes alike. Emotionally grounded and peaceful.

entries.name: Neutral Guardian
entries.description: The quiet heart of the group. Protects without ego, speaks with compassion, and walks the path of kindness.

entries.name: Neutral Defender
entries.description: Prioritizes safety over ideology. May not preach morality, but their actions guard the innocent.

entries.name: Neutral Arbiter
entries.description: A watcher of balance and need. Neither law-bound nor wild, this figure serves the people - however that must look.

entries.name: Neutral Sentinel
entries.description: Honors a code of protection and patience. Acts when needed, guards without words, and never asks for praise.

entries.name: Neutral Enforcer
entries.description: Punches through problems so others don’t have to. Brutal, efficient, but undeniably selfless.

entries.name: Neutral Vigilante
entries.description: Stalks the wicked to defend the helpless. Walks the line between justice and vengeance.

entries.name: Neutral Crusader
entries.description: Champions the cause without borders. Fights for those who cannot, loyal only to their personal sense of good.

entries.name: Chaotic Coordinator
entries.description: Leads with heart and improvisation. Makes peace in wild ways - might build a shelter and overthrow the mayor.

entries.name: Chaotic Mediator
entries.description: The unconventional diplomat. Defuses tension with surprise hugs, strange jokes, or unexpected wisdom.

entries.name: Chaotic Guardian
entries.description: A wild protector with a golden heart. Thinks laws are optional, but kindness is sacred.

entries.name: Chaotic Defender
entries.description: Brings safety through unexpected means. May cause a little chaos to save a lot of lives.

entries.name: Chaotic Arbiter
entries.description: A whimsical judge of right and wrong. Morals fluid, heart steady - they fight for people, not systems.

entries.name: Chaotic Sentinel
entries.description: Fights with passion and principle. Disregards rules - but never their personal honor.

entries.name: Chaotic Enforcer
entries.description: Punches down walls to lift people up. Violent but well-meaning - a wrecking ball for good.

entries.name: Chaotic Vigilante
entries.description: A storm of justice. Protects others even when it means crossing lines, breaking rules, or being feared.

entries.name: Chaotic Crusader
entries.description: A freedom fighter wrapped in fire. Wields chaos in service of compassion. Unpredictable, unwavering.

matrix_notes.note: The attached guide documents 62 profile entries. The fully neutral Neutral-Neutral-Neutral-Neutral slot is not named in the guide, so it is listed as missing rather than invented.
